items.headline: Opposition politician Lim Tean handed three fresh charges for absconding while on bail
items.summary: Opposition politician Lim Tean faced three new charges over allegedly fleeing Singapore while on bail, taking his tally to seven; a pre-trial conference was fixed for Oct 23.

items.headline: Lee Biscuits to end production and close its factory after 92 years
items.summary: Lee Biscuits, the 92-year-old maker of Marie biscuits, will stop manufacturing and shut its Pontian, Johor factory by end-October as its parent consolidates around rubber and palm oil.

items.headline: Man jailed 18 months for emailing an intimate video of his ex-girlfriend to her colleagues
items.summary: A 40-year-old man was sentenced on Oct 22 to 18 months' jail for distributing an intimate video of his former girlfriend to her colleagues and bosses, and ordered to pay S$1,500 compensation.

items.headline: Man fined S$7,000 for running an unlicensed massage parlour at Orchard Towers
items.summary: A 65-year-old Singaporean was fined S$7,000 for operating an unlicensed Orchard Towers massage parlour where his wife offered sexual services, after pleading guilty to one charge.

items.headline: Update: Jio Platforms closes India's largest rupee IPO with heavy demand, listing set for Oct 28
items.summary: Reliance's Jio Platforms closed its three-day bidding window with heavy demand, drawing anchor bids topping US$26 billion; the roughly US$108 billion offering, India's largest rupee IPO, lists Oct 28.

items.headline: US presses Reliance to refine more Venezuelan crude as Rubio tours the Jamnagar plant
items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio toured Reliance's 1.4 million bpd Jamnagar refinery and said its capacity could help Washington's push for India to refine more Venezuelan crude; Reliance is the top buyer of Venezuelan oil outside the US.

items.headline: India's central bank tightens scrutiny of large overseas investments to curb capital outflows
items.summary: India's central bank has reportedly stepped up scrutiny of large overseas investments by domestic companies to contain capital outflows amid pressure on the rupee, Bloomberg reported.

items.headline: Update: Rupee extends its rally to an eighth session, its strongest since June, on Jio IPO inflows
items.summary: The rupee extended gains to an eighth straight session, its longest winning run since January 2024, closing near 94.45 per dollar - its strongest since June 25 - on foreign inflows into the Jio IPO.

items.headline: UK retail sales fell 0.4% in September, worse than expected before the Budget
items.summary: British retail sales volumes dropped 0.4% in September, worse than the 0.1% dip forecast, as a warm month hit clothing and cost-of-living pressures squeezed spending before the Oct 28 Budget.

items.headline: UK consumer confidence slumps 11 points to minus 24, the steepest monthly drop since the pandemic
items.summary: The GfK consumer-confidence index fell 11 points to minus 24 in October, its sharpest one-month decline since the pandemic, a drop Bloomberg likened to the Brexit-era shock.

items.headline: UK private-sector activity unexpectedly quickens as the composite PMI rises to 53.1
items.summary: UK private-sector output picked up in October, with the S&P Global flash composite PMI rising to 53.1 and beating forecasts in services and manufacturing - a rare bright spot before the Budget.

items.headline: Investors warm to UK gilts, betting on a disciplined first Budget from Chancellor Healey
items.summary: Fund managers including Rathbones have been buying longer-dated UK gilts, betting Chancellor John Healey will keep spending disciplined in his Oct 28 Budget, after 30-year yields briefly touched 6% this month.

items.headline: Update: Russia and Ukraine agree to resume peace talks in Abu Dhabi in early November
items.summary: The Kremlin said Russia and Ukraine will hold US-mediated trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November, after envoy Steve Witkoff met Putin; Al Jazeera said hopes for a breakthrough are slim.

items.headline: Update: WHO warns of a 'more complex' Ebola outbreak now spanning three African countries
items.summary: The WHO warned of a 'more complex' Ebola outbreak across three African countries after Nigeria confirmed a case in Abuja linked to the DR Congo strain, adding to infections in Kenya.

items.headline: Ultra-Orthodox military conscription dominates Israel's election battleground before the Oct 27 vote
items.summary: With Israel's election set for Oct 27, the campaign is being driven by a bitter debate over whether the ultra-Orthodox minority should be conscripted into military service.

items.headline: Israel plans a full West Bank lockdown after a deadly gunfight near Hebron
items.summary: Israel said it would impose a full lockdown of the occupied West Bank and arrested 36 Palestinians after a deadly gunfight near Hebron, as raids on farming communities intensified.

items.headline: Nvidia's open-source 'Microduck' robots top 20,000 pre-orders after a GTC Berlin demo
items.summary: Open-source 'Microduck' robots, built by Hugging Face's Pollen Robotics, drew more than 20,000 pre-orders after Nvidia chief Jensen Huang played with them during a GTC Berlin keynote.

items.headline: Tesla begins early production of its Optimus humanoid robot in California
items.summary: Tesla has started what Elon Musk called 'early production' of its Optimus humanoid robot in Fremont, California, though he warned the ramp would be slow; it still targets 20,000 units a week by late 2027.

items.headline: Physical-AI start-up Eka Robotics raises US$150 million at a US$1.45 billion valuation
items.summary: Physical-AI start-up Eka Robotics closed a US$150 million Series A at a US$1.45 billion post-money valuation, led by a16z and F-Prime; its robot can pick about 1,500 objects an hour.

items.headline: AI assistant start-up Town hits a unicorn valuation with a US$108 million Series B
items.summary: Town, an AI assistant start-up just four months old, reached a unicorn valuation with a US$108 million Series B co-led by Forerunner Ventures and Menlo Ventures.

items.headline: Procter & Gamble beats on fiscal first-quarter earnings as organic sales rise 4%
items.summary: Procter & Gamble beat on its fiscal first quarter, posting core EPS of US$2.00 on US$23.28 billion in revenue as organic sales rose 4%; shares climbed about 5%.

items.headline: American Express to cut about 5% of its workforce to 'prepare for AI'
items.summary: American Express said it would cut about 5% of its global workforce - roughly 3,500 roles - and take a US$336 million charge to reorganize around AI; quarterly profit beat estimates but shares fell about 3%.

items.headline: Wall Street sells off as the Dow drops 653 points and oil tops US$100
items.summary: US stocks fell on Oct 23, with the Dow sliding 652.82 points (1.2%) to 52,215.16, as oil pushed above US$100 a barrel on fears the US-Iran conflict could reignite.

items.headline: Gold heads for its steepest weekly loss since June as oil fuels Fed rate worries
items.summary: Gold was on track for its worst week since June, easing toward US$4,016 an ounce as surging oil prices reinforced expectations the Federal Reserve will keep rates higher for longer.

items.headline: India pull off a record T20I chase to beat New Zealand in the Christchurch opener
items.summary: India opened their New Zealand tour with a record T20I chase in Christchurch, reaching 230 for 6 to overhaul the hosts' 225 for 4 and win by four wickets, led by Samson, Iyer and Dhir.

items.headline: Leclerc tops first practice for the US Grand Prix as Verstappen's quickest lap is deleted
items.summary: Charles Leclerc set the fastest time in opening practice for the US Grand Prix at Austin, edging Max Verstappen by 0.084s - Verstappen's quickest lap was later deleted for track limits - with Norris third.

items.headline: Antonelli can clinch a maiden F1 title at Sunday's US Grand Prix in Austin
items.summary: Leader Kimi Antonelli, on 340 points, can seal his first F1 title at Sunday's US Grand Prix if he wins with George Russell ninth or lower and Lewis Hamilton fifth or lower; otherwise it rolls on to Mexico.

items.headline: Rybakina leads the WTA Finals race as the eight-woman field heads to Indian Wells
items.summary: Elena Rybakina topped the WTA Finals Race as the eight-woman field was confirmed for the finale at Indian Wells from Nov 8; Aryna Sabalenka is set to be seeded second, while Iga Swiatek will miss the event.

items.headline: Astronomers match the stars in Van Gogh's 'The Starry Night' to the Hyades cluster
items.summary: Writing in Scientific Reports, researchers said the swirling stars in Van Gogh's 'The Starry Night' match the V-shaped Hyades cluster in Taurus as it appeared over Saint-Remy on 22 July 1889.

items.headline: NASA revises its Thwaites 'Doomsday' Glacier forecast, warning of faster sea-level rise
items.summary: A NASA study refined projections for Antarctica's Thwaites 'Doomsday' Glacier, finding it could contribute more to sea-level rise by the end of the century than some earlier estimates.

items.headline: NASA's Perseverance sets an off-world driving record, passing Opportunity's distance on Mars
items.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover set an off-world driving record on Mars, its odometer reaching 28.10 miles (45.22 km) to pass Opportunity's mark, having driven over 90% of that distance autonomously.

items.headline: Scientists turn cloned male mouse embryos into fertile females in a first for genetics
items.summary: Researchers used a CRISPR-based 'Y-CUT' technique to turn cloned male mouse embryos into healthy, fertile females - a first that could aid efforts to rescue endangered species with few survivors.

fun_fact.headline: A teaspoon of neutron-star material would weigh about a billion tonnes
fun_fact.body: A single teaspoon of neutron-star material would weigh roughly a billion tonnes on Earth - about the mass of a mountain. Neutron stars cram more than the Sun's mass into a sphere only about 20 kilometres across, making them the densest objects known short of black holes.

puzzle.title: Split the Bill
puzzle.body: A group of friends split a restaurant bill equally. Had there been 2 more friends, each would have paid $6 less; had there been 3 fewer friends, each would have paid $12 more. How many friends were there, and what was the total bill?
puzzle.approach: Let the group size be n and the total bill T, then turn each 'what if' into an equation and solve the pair.
puzzle.answer: 18 friends, total bill $1,080 (each paid $60). T/(n+2)=T/n-6 gives T=3n(n+2); T/(n-3)=T/n+12 gives T=4n(n-3); equating, 3(n+2)=4(n-3), so n=18 and T=1,080.

word_puzzle.title: Cross Purposes
word_puzzle.body: Sort 16 words into four groups of four: JAB, HOOK, CARP, CROP, MULLET, BREAM, WHINE, CROSS, FADE, TROUT, GRIPE, UPPERCUT, PERM, PIKE, BEEF, MOAN.
word_puzzle.approach: Sort the 16 words into four groups of four; one word in each group looks like it belongs elsewhere.
word_puzzle.answer: Boxing punches: JAB, HOOK, CROSS, UPPERCUT. Hairstyles: CROP, FADE, MULLET, PERM. Freshwater fish: CARP, BREAM, TROUT, PIKE. Ways to complain: WHINE, GRIPE, BEEF, MOAN.
